newsitem.title: USA: Dean Foods vegetable results may hurt Q2.
newsitem.headline: Dean Foods vegetable results may hurt Q2.

text.p: Dean Foods Co said Thursday results from its vegetable operations could be a drag on its fiscal second quarter results, although it expects a good crop harvest this year to lead to improved results for fiscal 1997.
"Right now, yes, the second quarter will probably be effected, but earnings will improve going forward," Dean Foods Chairman Howard Dean said on a teleconference in response to a question.

The only potential concern for vegetable supplies is corn, which has been effected by late planting, Tom Rose, company president said. "An early frost could have a pretty significant effect on that volume," Rose said. "We need a good fall to get a good corn crop."
Dean Foods executives said that despite tighter raw milk supplies in the United States the company has been able to secure adequate supplies.
U.S. milk supplies are down three to four percent versus last year due to higher feed costs and dairy herd cutbacks.

"Raw milk prices continue to escalate and are estimated to increase further into October and November. Butterfat also is projected to increase over that same period," Rose said. In December, he added, butterfat prices are expected to drop.
Despite the higher milk costs, Dean Foods executives said the company has been able to maintain its margins.
Rose said Dean's ice cream sales were down about six percent, comparable with the industry, which he linked to higher retail prices due to increased input costs.
He added that Dean's branded ice cream volume rose particularly in the Midwest and Southeast due to new products.
Earlier, Dean Foods reported record first quarter earnings of $0.45 a share compared with $0.43 a year ago.
"Our dairy, pickle and specialty businesses all outperformed last year's first quarter results, while the vegetable business performance was below last year's," Dean said in a statement.

He added the dairy segment benefited from volume and cost reductions, while the pickle business saw improved procurement and operating efficiencies. Specialty segment results reflected strong sales and earnings of its powdered products business.
